severity: published numbers wrong for a code reason; no conclusion changes
what_the_defect_is: The frame-C census runner looks up judge records with the literal task-id prefix `judge::r4c::`. Every later runner was DERIVED from it by frame rebinding, and that literal was not rebound, while each runner wrote its judge ids under its own mode (`r4d`, `r4e`). The lookup therefore matched nothing, every chunk failed the `judges_ok` test, and the thresholded endpoint V was published as 0 for every arm.
how_it_was_found: While rebinding the same runner for frame F, the mode segment was grepped across all four derived runners and found hardcoded to r4c in all of them; the actual judge ids on disk were then counted per prefix.
why_it_survived_review: V flooring at 0 was the expected result for this corpus -- the frames B/C discussion already predicted low visual necessity -- so a floored V looked like a measurement instead of a lookup failure. A plausible expected value is exactly the condition under which a silent bug is not noticed.

affected_runs.why_not: V floors in both readings: the largest corrected count is 1 of 60, every paired contrast stays at p=1.0, and V was reported as a SECONDARY endpoint in both frames. The published tables are wrong in the counts and right in the conclusion.
